reason: OpenAI organization administration (keys, users, projects, usage, audit logs, certificates, spend limits). Yunshu is a single-user local server: the admin API and multi-tenant RBAC were removed on purpose (CLAUDE.md refocus).
Project administration inside an OpenAI organization (roles, groups, service accounts, rate limits); there is no organization here.
Hosted fine-tuning jobs, checkpoints, permissions and graders. Yunshu is an inference engine; training is out of scope. LoRA adapters are loaded, not trained, here.
Deletes a fine-tuned model of the caller's organization; models here are local directories managed with the CLI.
Assistants API, deprecated by OpenAI in favour of Responses and Conversations (both served).
Threads and Runs belong to the deprecated Assistants API; Conversations and Responses replace them.
Hosted retrieval index behind file_search; there is no hosted vector store. Local retrieval is /v1/embeddings plus the caller's own index.
Multipart upload of files above the Files API size limit for hosted storage; the local Files store takes the file in one request.
Needs a hosted moderation classifier; no moderation model is shipped. /v1/classify serves a local classifier checkpoint for the same job.
Video generation (Sora) is a parked modality in this engine (CLAUDE.md: other modalities are supported capabilities, not the identity).
Hosted Code Interpreter sandboxes and their files; Yunshu runs no remote sandbox.
Subscriptions to OpenAI-hosted events (batch / response completed); a local server has no event bus. Clients poll or stream.
Catalogue for the hosted webhook subscriptions above.
Backend of OpenAI's hosted ChatKit widget (sessions, threads).
OpenAI's hosted safety alerts and cases for an organization.
Verifies OpenAI watermarks / C2PA on hosted generations; no generation is signed here.
Hosted credential vaults of the Agents platform.
OpenAI's managed Agents platform (sessions, environments, vaults, traces); hosted runtime. Agent workloads reach Yunshu through /v1/responses, MCP and the chat routes.
GPT-Live voice sessions, forks and sideband sockets; native voice is a parked modality (Realtime is served as a text turn).
Realtime speech translation sessions; voice is a parked modality.

WebRTC signalling (SDP offer in, answer out) for browsers; needs aiortc with its native codec stack, which is not in the dependency set, and a real audio round trip to verify (docs/guides/TRANSPORTS.md). The WebSocket path and the ephemeral client secrets that browsers use are served.
Accept / reject / refer / hangup of an inbound SIP call: a telephony trunk (Twilio, SIP webhooks) that a local server does not have.
Custom voice creation for speech; low priority (voice is parked).

Evals (create, runs, output items): a local grader runner over stored completions is a fit and is the next item after stored completions; string_check / text_similarity graders need no model, label_model / score_model use the loaded model. Not started.

Skills are versioned bundles mounted into OpenAI-hosted shell / code-execution containers. Yunshu has no hosted sandbox to mount them in, so a skill store would hold files nothing can run; local agents keep skills in their own checkout.
Anthropic Admin API (keys, users, invites, workspaces, rate limits, spend limits, RBAC, plugins, federation); admin was removed with multi-tenant control.

Agent Skills are uploaded bundles loaded into Anthropic-hosted code-execution containers (container.skills). Yunshu has no hosted sandbox; Claude Code-style agents load skills from their own filesystem.
Claude Managed Agents: hosted agent definitions and runtime.
Claude Managed Agents sessions, events and resources (hosted runtime).
Managed Agents execution environments (hosted sandboxes).
Hosted credential vaults of Managed Agents.
Hosted Memory stores of Managed Agents; local memory is the caller's own store.
Managed Agents background memory consolidation (hosted).
Managed Agents deployments (hosted). Hosted Anthropic service with no local counterpart in a single-node engine.
Managed Agents deployment runs (hosted).
Network tunnels for Managed Agents environments (hosted).
Hosted end-user profiles of the Managed Agents platform.
